title: Stocking-stitch scarf
subtitle: A smooth-faced scarf with a garter-stitch border to stop the curl.
excerpt: A flat scarf worked in stocking stitch (US: stockinette) with a two-stitch garter border on each edge to prevent curling, knitted on 4.5 mm needles with DK yarn. Finished dimensions are 20 cm wide by 175 cm long.
sourceNotes: Stocking stitch (also called stocking fabric) is described in Weldon's Practical Knitter as the standard knitting fabric: right-side rows knitted, wrong-side rows purled. The garter-stitch border method to prevent curling is documented throughout Weldon's. Cornelia Mee, A Manual of Knitting and Crochet (1846), Internet Archive.

glossaryTerms.definition: The fabric produced by alternating a knit row and a purl row. The right side shows smooth V-shaped loops; the wrong side shows horizontal purl ridges. Called stockinette in US terminology.
A cast-on method that forms a neat, elastic edge by using the tail and working yarn together over two fingers. Produces one row of knitting as it sets up.
The process of removing stitches from the needle to form a finished edge. Also called bind off in US terminology.
Wetting or steaming the finished knitted piece and pinning it to shape while it dries, to even the stitches and set the dimensions.

content.text: This is a flat scarf worked from cast-on to cast-off in stocking stitch (US: stockinette). A two-stitch garter border on each edge keeps the fabric from rolling inward. It finishes at 20 cm wide and 175 cm long. The smooth knit face reads neatly in plain or semi-solid yarns; the purl face is perfectly wearable and can be worn either way.

The scarf is worked flat in rows because stocking stitch in the round would make a tube, not a flat rectangle. Flat construction on straight needles is the simplest way to produce the smooth fabric of a stocking stitch scarf. The two-stitch garter border is included on each edge because unbordered stocking stitch curls: the knit rows pull the fabric toward the right side, and without a non-rolling border the finished scarf rolls into a tube around the edges. The scarf uses about 175 g (395 m / 432 yards) of DK-weight yarn.

items.name: DK-weight wool or wool-blend yarn
items.substitutions: Any DK yarn. Wool or wool-blend is recommended for warmth and elasticity.

items.name: 4.5 mm needles (UK 7 / US 7)
items.qty: 1 pair or 1 circular, 40 cm or longer

content.text: 20 sts x 28 rows = 10 x 10 cm in stocking stitch on 4.5 mm needles, blocked. Swatch over at least 25 stitches, measure across the central 10 stitches once the swatch has been blocked and dried. Each stitch off gauge shifts the finished width by about 1 cm: at 19 sts per 10 cm the scarf finishes 21 cm wide; at 21 sts it finishes 19 cm. Each two-row difference across the full 490-row scarf adds or removes about 7 cm of finished length.

K (knit): insert the right needle front-to-back through the first stitch, wrap the yarn, draw the loop through. P (purl): with the yarn in front, insert the right needle back-to-front, wrap the yarn, draw the loop through to the back.

, cast on 40 stitches. Tail length formula: tail_cm = (needle circumference in mm x stitch count) / 10 + 15. For a 4.5 mm needle (circumference approximately 14.1 mm) and 40 stitches: (14.1 x 40) / 10 + 15 = 56.4 + 15 = about 71 cm. Leave a tail of at least 71 cm.
Stitch count check-in: 40 stitches on the needle after the cast-on.

Repeat Rows 1 and 2 until the scarf measures 175 cm from the cast-on edge, measured along the straight grain with the piece lying flat. This takes approximately 490 rows. At the halfway mark (about 87 cm), count the stitches again: you should still have 40 stitches.
On a right-side row, use the standard

: K2, pass the first stitch over the second, K1, pass the second over. Continue to the last stitch, cut the yarn leaving a 15 cm tail, and pull through the final loop. The cast-off should be worked with the same tension as the body; if it pulls in, use a needle one size larger.

Edges curling even with the garter border. This usually means the garter border stitches are being worked in stocking stitch (knit on RS, purl on WS) instead of every row knitted. On WS rows the instruction is K2, P to last 2 sts, K2: all four border stitches are knitted on both RS and WS.

Extra stitches appearing. A yarn-over happens when the yarn is left in front at the start of a right-side row before the first knit stitch. Always check that the yarn is at the back before you insert the needle for the first knit.
Tight or puckered cast-off. Work the final row with a needle one size larger than the body needle so the cast-off edge stretches to match the body width.
Weave in both yarn tails along the wrong-side edge using the tapestry needle. Wet

is recommended for wool: soak in cool water for 20 minutes, press out moisture without wringing, roll in a towel, then pin flat and allow to dry overnight. The stocking stitch face will even out and the garter border will hold the edges flat.

Handwash wool in cool water with a small amount of wool wash. Support the wet weight and lay flat to dry. For cotton: machine wash gentle on a cool cycle and lay flat. For acrylic: cool gentle machine wash; do not tumble dry.

A stocking-stitch scarf in a semi-solid or gradient yarn shows the fabric at its best. The next step is a ribbed scarf, which replaces the stocking-stitch body with alternating knit and purl columns and produces a fabric that stretches across its width to hug the neck.
